spec.name: Earnings drift v24
spec.notes: Post-earnings drift on the reported surprise.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.8, annual return 8%, maximum drawdown 2%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.84 to 2.82 (change -0.01).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.84 to 2.84. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.76 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.84); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.84 against 2.84 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 2.10 against 2.84 in research, a gap of +0.73.
The best year gives 18% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 88%; Sharpe is 3.62 in calm and 1.21 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.03, so the claimed 2.80 becomes 2.77 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.91 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.51).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.84 to as low as 2.42 (as low as 2.59 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 20% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 13% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
